**Step 1 — Scene:** A meal of lasagne, mixed salad, a separate dressing cup, and a wrapped Magnum-style ice cream bar. Water contributes no energy and is excluded below.

**Step 2 — Vessels:** Estimated main plate diameter **24 cm**, area **452 cm²**; salad bowl diameter **21 cm**, area **346 cm²**. The dressing cup is approximately **5 cm** across, area **20 cm²**.

**Steps 3–6 — Items, coverage, volume and weight:** Coverage percentages refer to each item’s own vessel. Lasagne includes its visible pasta, sauce, vegetables and cheese.

| Item | Vessel coverage | Area × typical height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Lasagne | 42% of main plate | 190 × 2.0 = 380 ml | 0.90 g/ml | 342 g |
| Salad leaves | 50% of salad bowl | 173 × 2.5 = 433 ml | 0.15 g/ml | 65 g |
| Tomatoes | 15% of salad bowl | 52 × 1.5 = 78 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 47 g |
| Cucumber | 12% of salad bowl | 42 × 1.3 = 55 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 33 g |
| Carrot strips | 3% of salad bowl | 10 × 0.5 = 5 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 3 g |
| Dressing | 100% of cup footprint | 20 × 1.25 = 25 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 25 g |

The salad’s allocated coverage totals **80%**; the main plate is approximately **42% covered**. These are non-overlapping footprint allocations.

The wrapped ice cream cannot be measured directly; assuming it contains one standard chocolate-coated bar, estimate **85 g**, excluding packaging.

**Step 7 — Energy:** Using approximately 170 kcal/100 g for lasagne, 20 for leaves, 18 for tomatoes, 15 for cucumber, 41 for carrot, 350 for dressing, and 300 for the ice cream gives **about 960 kcal**.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Total edible weight is approximately **600 g**. A substantial lasagne portion, about 150 g of salad, dressing and one ice cream bar plausibly fit the scene. Lasagne composition, dressing oil content and the concealed bar are the largest uncertainties.
